chapter_name: Shabd Vichar: Srot, Rachna, Aur Arth Ke Aadhar Par (Morphology)
learning_objective: 🎯 By the end of this chapter, you will uncover the hidden history of Hindi words, learn how they are built, and categorize them like a true linguist!

main_concepts.concept_title: 🔤 What is a Shabd? (The Meaningful Team)
main_concepts.simple_explanation: A group of letters (Varn) that makes complete sense is called a Shabd (Word). If you join 'क', 'म', and 'ल', it makes 'कमल' (Lotus) - a valid word. But if you join 'ल', 'म', 'क', it makes 'लमक' - which means nothing, so it is not a word!

main_concepts.concept_title: 🧬 Srot Ke Aadhar Par (Where did the word come from?)
main_concepts.simple_explanation: Based on origin, words are categorized: 'Tatsam' (Copy-pasted from Sanskrit, like 'Surya'), 'Tadbhav' (Sanskrit words that changed over time, like Surya became 'Sooraj'), 'Deshaj' (Born in local Indian villages, like 'Lota' or 'Jhadu'), and 'Videshi' (Travelled from other countries, like 'Doctor' or 'Station').

main_concepts.concept_title: 🧱 Rachna Ke Aadhar Par (How is the word built?)
main_concepts.simple_explanation: Based on structure: 'Roorh' words are solid basics that can't be broken (like 'Ghar' or 'Jal'). 'Yaugik' words are made by joining two words (like 'Rasoi' + 'Ghar' = 'Rasoighar'). 'Yogroorh' words are joined words but point to a VIP special meaning (like 'Pankaj' literally means 'born in mud', but only means Lotus).

main_concepts.concept_title: 🎭 Arth Ke Aadhar Par (What does the word mean?)
main_concepts.simple_explanation: Words can also be sorted by meaning. This includes 'Paryayvachi' (Synonyms - different words, same meaning), 'Vilom' (Antonyms - opposite meanings), 'Ekarthi' (Words with exactly one meaning), and 'Anekarthi' (One word, multiple meanings, like 'Teer' = arrow OR river bank).

When words enter a sentence, they get a job. 'Vikari' (Changeable) words change their form based on gender, number, or tense (Noun, Pronoun, Verb). 'Avikari' (Unchangeable) words act stubborn and never change their form, no matter what (like 'aur', 'kintu', 'dheere').

fun_activity.title: 🌍 The 'Foreign Word' Detective
fun_activity.instructions: Did you know you speak foreign languages every day? Find 5 'Videshi' (foreign) words in your house right now! (Hint: Look for things like a 'Machine', 'Table', 'Pen', or 'Cup'). Write them down and guess which language they came from!

quick_recap: ⭐ A word (Shabd) is a meaningful combination of letters.
⭐ Origin (Srot): Words can be Tatsam (Sanskrit), Tadbhav (changed Sanskrit), Deshaj (local), or Videshi (foreign).
⭐ Structure (Rachna): Words can be Roorh (basic), Yaugik (compound), or Yogroorh (compound with special meaning).
⭐ Meaning (Arth): Words are classified into Synonyms, Antonyms, Single-meaning, and Multi-meaning.
⭐ Usage (Prayog): Vikari words change form based on grammar; Avikari words never change.
